paragraphs.text: On the model axis, the recorded explicit-stance belief positive control is moderate for the smaller model and small for the larger model, with both intervals excluding zero. The smaller-model arm is dose-matched to the larger-model arm and differs only by model; the larger-model control was retrained, and its separately calibrated gate threshold replaces rather than reuses the smaller-model bar. Action diverges: the smaller-model positive-control contrast is near zero and includes zero, precluding a conduction ratio, whereas the larger-model contrast is small and excludes zero. Its direction replicates at the paired seed, but substantial cross-seed scatter precludes magnitude generalization. Under full fine-tuning, the evidence-corpus belief contrast is near zero and excludes zero in both the first declared seed and its seed-matched paired seed with a re-derived schedule. Because the same corpus under LoRA straddles zero on probability while excluding zero on log-odds, this is interpreted as scale dependence rather than a capacity cliff.
